statement: Let b=(b0,b1,b2,b3) and a=(a0,a1,a2,a3) be ordered elements of Z_{>0}^4 satisfying the four-equation P4/Paw coefficient system (3.3) reproduced verbatim in source.md, and let s=sum_i b_i=sum_i a_i. Then the least possible s is 61. At s=61 the complete ordered solution set is the four Cartesian combinations b in {(1,16,8,36),(36,8,16,1)} and a in {(4,9,16,32),(4,16,9,32)}. All four have signature (61,1116,6912,18432), and they constitute one orbit under exactly the two allowed involutions b -> (b3,b2,b1,b0) and a -> (a0,a2,a1,a3). The scope is only the least positive layer of this fixed coefficient system; it does not determine the minimum order among all connected distance-cospectral graph pairs or classify solutions above sum 61.
contribution: This completely resolves the frozen least-layer problem that the cited source's order-61 witness leaves open: two exact, structurally different finite verifiers establish absence through sum 60 and completeness of the four ordered solutions at 61. One verifier exhaustively joins arbitrary-precision integer signatures over all 521855 positive ordered quadruples per side; the other directly exhausts a sound bounded QF_BV encoding and terminates UNSAT after blocking its four models. A dated targeted primary-literature search found no equivalent result, but no claim of priority is made beyond that limited search.
